messages:
Harper (People Ops): Heads up  updated travel & safety guidance goes live 2026-09-01. Key changes: (1) expanded emergency evacuation reimbursement cap (now up to $5k per incident), (2) mandatory travel safety training for international trips >72hrs, and (3) refreshed conduct expectations for vendor-hosted events. Full doc below.

Sam (People Ops): Why the reimbursement increase?

Harper (People Ops): We reviewed recent incidents and partner costs. The higher cap helps cover unplanned repatriation and emergency lodging. Finance and Insurance okayed it.

Noah (Legal): Note: evacuation payments may be taxable in some jurisdictions. We're recommending managers coordinate with Payroll and Legal for unusual cases.

Olivia (Recruiting): Will this change how we book candidate travel? We often book short city visits where safety training seems heavy.

Harper (People Ops): Candidate and recruiter travel remains on the old playbook for interviews. The mandatory safety training threshold only applies to business travel where a headcount is traveling internationally for >72 hours (e.g., multi-day conferences, on-site engagements).

Theo (Eng): Safety training  is this a live session or e-learning? Time commitment?

Sam (People Ops): It's a 45-minute recorded module + a short quiz (5 questions). Certificate issued on completion and valid for 24 months. We're also scheduling quarterly live Q&A drop-ins.

HR-bot: Policy doc: https://intranet.redwood/workplace/policies/travel-safety-2026. Training: https://learning.redwood/travel-safety.

Noah (Legal): Also adding a vendor-event clause: employees at vendor-sponsored off-site events must follow Redwood conduct policy. If an event is in a high-risk region, approval from Legal + People Ops required before travel is booked.

Olivia (Recruiting): OK good to know. Any changes to per-diem or meal allowances?

Harper (People Ops): Per-diem unchanged. We did add a discretionary allowance for airport overnight stays if flights are delayed due to carrier cancellations.

Theo (Eng): Who signs off on emergency evacuation reimbursements? Manager or People Ops?

Sam (People Ops): Manager initiates the request, People Ops approves for amounts under $2k; anything above goes to People Ops + Finance review. Insurance claims are separate and should be filed in parallel.

Noah (Legal): We'll update the vendor/contract annex templates to reflect the conduct expectation.

Harper (People Ops): Timeline: policy published 2026-08-01 (preview), feedback window through 2026-08-15, final effective 2026-09-01. Manager briefing 2026-08-10.

Olivia (Recruiting): Can we get a 1-pager to share with candidates who ask about safety?

Harper (People Ops): Yes  we'll produce a candidate-friendly FAQ and short slide deck for recruiters by 2026-08-05.

Theo (Eng): :thumbsup: Thanks.

Harper (People Ops): Thanks everyone. Post questions here or DM Sam/Noah for legal edge cases.

Sam (People Ops): FYI we're tracking feedback in the policy doc comments; please add inline notes if you see issues.
